chains.title: TCF7L2-bound ref G enhancer activates MYC
chains.cell_type: HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells / colon epithelial lineage

links.claim: TCF7L2, selected within the TCF/LEF QBiC-SELEX specificity group using colon/HCT116 expression and known Wnt/TCF biology, binds the ref G allele more strongly than alt T at rs6983267; QBiC-SELEX coverage not_checked.
The variant lies in a distal 8q24 enhancer whose activity is higher on the ref G allele.
The ref G enhancer increases MYC expression.
This occurs in colorectal carcinoma cells such as HCT116, consistent with the stated expression context.
Increased MYC expression raises colorectal cancer risk.

predictions: ref G shows stronger TCF7L2 binding than alt T
ref G shows higher enhancer activity than alt T
ref G associates with higher MYC expression in HCT116
knockdown of TCF7L2 reduces the allele-specific enhancer effect
falsified_if: Allele-specific TCF7L2 binding is absent or alt T binds TCF7L2 more strongly.
The rs6983267 region does not show allele-dependent enhancer activity in HCT116 cells.
MYC is not affected by the rs6983267 enhancer in colorectal cells.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs6983267
predictions: No allele-specific TF binding at rs6983267
No allele-specific enhancer activity attributable to rs6983267
Any association with MYC or colorectal cancer is due to a linked causal variant or another non-TF mechanism
falsified_if: Allele-specific TF binding and enhancer activity at rs6983267 are demonstrated in HCT116 cells.
MYC expression is shown to be causally affected by the rs6983267 allele.

chains.title: TCF7L2-bound alt T enhancer activates MYC
chains.cell_type: HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells / colon epithelial lineage

links.claim: TCF7L2, selected within the TCF/LEF QBiC-SELEX specificity group, binds the alt T allele more strongly than ref G at rs6983267; QBiC-SELEX coverage not_checked.
The rs6983267 alt T allele creates a stronger 8q24 enhancer in colorectal cells.
The alt T enhancer increases MYC expression.
This occurs in HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells.
Higher MYC expression raises colorectal cancer risk.

predictions: alt T shows stronger TCF7L2 binding than ref G
alt T shows higher enhancer activity than ref G
alt T associates with higher MYC expression in HCT116
TCF7L2 knockdown reduces the alt T-specific enhancer effect
falsified_if: TCF7L2 binds ref G more strongly than alt T.
Alt T does not increase enhancer activity or MYC expression.
TCF7L2 knockdown does not change the alt T-specific effect.

chains.title: LEF1-bound ref G enhancer activates MYC
chains.cell_type: HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells / colon epithelial lineage

links.claim: LEF1, another TCF/LEF family factor, binds the ref G allele more strongly than alt T at rs6983267; QBiC-SELEX coverage not_checked. This chain is less favored because TCF7L2 is the better-supported colorectal Wnt factor.
The ref G allele increases 8q24 enhancer activity through LEF1.
LEF1-bound enhancer activity increases MYC expression.
This occurs in HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells.
Increased MYC expression raises colorectal cancer risk.

predictions: LEF1, not TCF7L2, shows the stronger allele-specific binding
LEF1 knockdown reduces enhancer activity and MYC expression
ref G shows higher enhancer activity than alt T
falsified_if: LEF1 does not bind the rs6983267 region allele-specifically in HCT116 cells.
The enhancer effect is not LEF1-dependent.
MYC is not the target gene.

matrix.test: Allele-specific TCF7L2 EMSA with ref G and alt T probes using HCT116 nuclear extract, with anti-TCF7L2 supershift

outcomes.outcome: ref G > alt T TCF7L2 binding supports chain1
alt T > ref G TCF7L2 binding supports chain2

next_experiment: Cheapest single experiment separating chain1 from the null: allele-specific TCF7L2 EMSA using ref G and alt T probes with HCT116 nuclear extract and anti-TCF7L2 supershift. If ref G binds TCF7L2 more strongly, chain1 is supported and the null and opposite-direction chain2 are disfavored; if there is no allele-specific binding, the null is favored. A follow-up luciferase/reporter assay would test enhancer activity rather than binding alone.
